q: In Ecclesiastes, the Teacher says to everything there is a what?
why: A time for every purpose under heaven.
quote: To everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven

q: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to plant and a time to do what?
why: Life has its seasons.
quote: a time to plant and a time to uproot

q: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to weep and a time to do what?
why: Both sorrow and joy have their time.
quote: a time to weep and a time to laugh

q: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to mourn and a time to do what?
why: Sadness does not last forever.
quote: a time to mourn and a time to dance

q: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to be silent and a time to do what?
why: Wisdom knows when to talk.
quote: a time to be silent and a time to speak

q: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time for war and a time for what?
why: Everything has its time.
quote: a time for war and a time for peace.

q: In Ecclesiastes, what has God made beautiful in its time?
why: He set eternity in our hearts.
quote: He has made everything beautiful in its time.

q: Who is the Teacher whose words fill Ecclesiastes?
why: He was king in Jerusalem.
quote: These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem

q: What does the Teacher in Ecclesiastes say everything is?
why: Life without God has no lasting meaning.
quote: Everything is futile!

q: According to the Teacher in Ecclesiastes, there is nothing new where?
why: What has been will be again.
quote: there is nothing new under the sun.

q: In Ecclesiastes, why are two better than one?
why: If one falls, the other lifts him up.
quote: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up

q: In Ecclesiastes, what kind of cord is not quickly broken?
why: Together we are stronger.
quote: Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.

q: In Ecclesiastes, since God is in heaven and you are on earth, how should your words be?
why: Do not be quick to speak.
quote: So let your words be few.

q: In Ecclesiastes, what is never satisfied by money?
why: Loving wealth brings no rest.
quote: He who loves money is never satisfied by money

q: In Ecclesiastes, when should you remember your Creator?
a: In the days of your youth
why: Before hard days come.
quote: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth

q: How does the Teacher sum up everything at the end of Ecclesiastes?
why: It is the whole duty of man.
quote: Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man.

q: In Ecclesiastes, how should you do whatever your hands find to do?
why: Life's time is limited.
quote: Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might

q: Over what was the Teacher of Ecclesiastes king?
why: He was David's son.
quote: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

q: In Ecclesiastes, what has God set in the hearts of men?
why: Yet we cannot fathom all God's work.
quote: He has also set eternity in the hearts of men

q: In Ecclesiastes, a patient spirit is better than what?
why: The end is better than the beginning.
quote: and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.

q: In Ecclesiastes, what are we told to cast upon the waters?
why: After many days you will find it again.
quote: Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.

q: In Ecclesiastes, there is a time to cast away stones and a time to do what?
why: Everything has its time.
quote: a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together
